chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Amr al-Shami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed, the number of months in the presence of God is twelve months in the Book of God, from the day He created the heavens and the earth.
So the foremost of the months is the Month of God — Mighty is His mention — and it is the Month of Ramadan.
And the heart of the Month of Ramadan is the Night of Power (Laylat al-Qadr).
And the Quran was revealed in the first night of the Month of Ramadan. Therefore, welcome the month with the Quran.

key_terms.شَهْرُ اللَّهِ: Month of God — a special appellation for Ramadan indicating divine ownership and supreme sanctity
key_terms.عَزَّ ذِكْرُهُ: Mighty is His mention — an honorific formula used when mentioning God
key_terms.غُرَّةُ الشُّهُورِ: The foremost/most noble of months; 'ghurra' refers to the white spot on a horse's forehead, signifying distinction and preeminence
key_terms.لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ: Night of Power/Destiny — the most blessed night of the year, when the Quran was first revealed

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the special status of Ramadan and Laylat al-Qadr?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) cites Quran 9:36 to establish the divine ordinance of twelve months, then identifies Ramadan as the supreme month — the 'Month of God' — and Laylat al-Qadr as its spiritual center. The hadith connects Ramadan's primacy to the revelation of the Quran therein and concludes with a practical directive: the proper way to greet Ramadan is through engagement with the Quran. This teaching would have resonated with early Shia Muslims who placed great emphasis on both Quranic recitation and the special status of Imam-endorsed religious practice.
